Big Garage Shortlist

Companion to the Western Relocation Atlas · listings read October 9, 2026

Big Garage Shortlist

For-sale homes between $300k and $950k with a large detached garage, shop or outbuilding, in the Denver, Boulder and Fort Collins areas and the foothills around them, plus a first look at the Seattle area. The garage columns hold only what the listing says; a question mark means it doesn't say. Each home is also scored on its neighborhood with the atlas criteria, and the weights recalculate the scores.

    How to read it

    • Size is the listing's own figure. Square feet are worked out from dimensions where given (30×40 ft is 1,200 sq ft). "Large" means the listing says so without a number. The size column sorts by square feet.
    • 220V is Y when the listing mentions 220 or 240 volt power, and "Power" when it only says the building has electricity. Doors counts overhead doors where stated. RV door is Y for an RV door or a door 12 ft or taller.
    • ADU is "Maybe" where the listing mentions a bunkhouse, studio or office in an outbuilding. None of these homes is on the ADU shortlist.
    • Detached not confirmed marks a few large garages where the listing never says the building is separate from the house.
    • Coverage. Two capped passes: the first aimed at the foothills and larger-lot suburbs; the second added Aurora, Brighton, Parker, Elizabeth and the Weld County towns (Erie, Frederick, Mead, Platteville, Fort Lupton, Windsor). The "Eastern plains" listings (Strasburg, Byers, Bennett, Deer Trail) sit outside the metros you asked for and are kept as their own region so you can hide them. Expect misses in dense Denver and Thornton.
    • Seattle area. One small capped pass (12 searches, 30 listing reads, then 8 leftover leads) aimed at the better-scoring outer towns in King and Snohomish counties, with a single search in Pierce County. Treat it as a sample, not a sweep. The map has a separate Seattle view.
    • Walkable core. Replaces plain walkability. It scores access to a walkable town centre, not whether the home’s own street is walkable: full credit within about a 20-minute bike ride (5 km), fading out by about a 10–15 minute drive (15 km). A big downtown counts fully; a small main street counts less, by an amount you set with Small-core credit in Weights (60% to start). Shown as access out of 100, not a percentile. Hover a cell for the core it uses. Weighted 4 by default.
    • Schools. Test results of the public schools within 3 km (the district average where none is that close): how many grade levels above or below the U.S. average students score in grades 3–8, 2009–19, from Stanford’s Education Data Archive. Percentile among 15,188 western neighborhoods. Scores track family income closely, so read them alongside Growth.
    • Growth. How much those same students improve each year from grade 3 to 8, compared with the U.S. average rate. It reflects the schools more than who lives nearby, and it often disagrees with Schools. Percentile across Colorado, Utah and Washington.
    • Pre-K. Two numbers for children under 6. Top: Montessori, Waldorf, Reggio-inspired and nature-based programs nearby. Bottom: top-rated programs nearby (NAEYC-accredited, Colorado Shines 4–5, Washington Early Achievers 4–5). Percentiles within each state, since the states rate differently; Utah’s bottom number counts NAEYC only.
    • K–8. Public and charter Montessori, Waldorf-method, EL Education and IB Primary Years schools within about a 20-minute drive. Percentile across all three states. None of these lists has a public program in Seattle itself.
    • School weights. Hover any school number for counts and details. Growth, Pre-K and K–8 start at zero in Weights, so they change the score only if you turn them up.
    • Garages under about 600 sq ft were dropped. Redfin does not show the MLS garage tags (220 Volt, Oversized Door, RV Garage), so blanks here mean the listing text is silent, not that the feature is absent. Prices and status are as read on October 9, 2026, mostly from Redfin. County records rarely list outbuildings, so ask the seller for the building's size, power, door heights and permits.

    How this was put together

    I searched Redfin listing descriptions for words like shop, workshop, outbuilding, RV, 220, pole barn and Quonset, on lots of a quarter acre or more, priced $300k–$950k. I read each listing and kept homes with a detached (or probably detached) building that holds vehicles and is at least 600 sq ft, holds three or more cars, or has an RV door. The garage columns record only what the listing says. The Seattle-area homes came from smaller capped passes, partly through agent listing sites. Each home is placed in its 2010 census tract and given that neighborhood’s scores from the Western Relocation Atlas: seven criteria, each a percentile among 15,188 western neighborhoods, combined with the weights you set. Walkable core measures distance to the nearest walkable town centre (the atlas’s town centres where the national walkability index is at least 10 of 20), scaled by how many such neighborhoods lie within 2 km of it. Schools uses Stanford’s Education Data Archive, which puts every public school’s test results on one national scale. Growth, from the same archive, measures how much students improve from grade 3 to 8, which says more about the schools themselves and less about who lives nearby. Rank compares the neighborhood with every other one in the same metro that fits the $300k–$950k budget and has an airline airport within about 100 km. K–8 counts public and charter Montessori, Waldorf-method, EL Education and IB Primary Years schools from their own directories. Preschool access counts licensed programs from the Colorado and Washington state files, Utah directories and NAEYC’s accredited list, with nearer programs counting more. Searches were capped to keep costs down, so treat each list as a strong sample rather than a complete census, and check the listing before acting on a row.

    How the areas compare on schools

    The typical (median) neighborhood in each area that fits the budget and airport rules, on each school measure. Overall is the plain average of the four, with Pre-K’s two numbers (play-based · top-rated) counted as one. Pre-K percentiles are measured within each state, so compare them only between areas in the same state. Bellingham has no listings on this page yet and is shown for reference.
